title: K-flat counit normalization of the cone connecting map
statement: Let f:Z→Y be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of Noetherian schemes, with the recorded derived categories D(O_Y) and D(O_Z) [def-pc-derived-category] in a common localization universe. Let F=Lf* be the recorded derived pullback [def-pc-derived-pullback], supplied with a strong monoidal structure for the recorded derived tensors [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. Let E=f* be the actual termwise module tensor-pullback functor [def-pc-module-pullback], assumed additive, and H its induced homotopy-category functor. Write Qh_X for the derived localization and c_X(K):O_X[1]⊗K≅K[1] for the canonical shift-unit comparison [def-sc-scheme-canonical-shift-unit-iso]. There exist e:F(O_Y[1])≅O_Z[1] and a natural transformation epsilon:Qh_Y⋙F→H⋙Qh_Z such that epsilon is invertible on every homotopy object represented by a K-flat complex [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For every morphism p:P→Q between K-flat complexes, set C=mappingCone.triangleh(p), T=Qh_Y.mapTriangle(C), and W=(H⋙Qh_Z).mapTriangle(C). Then epsilon(C.obj3)≫W.mor3 = F(T.mor3)≫a(T.obj1)≫epsilon(C.obj1)[1], where a(K) is the composite F(c_Y(K) inverse), the supplied inverse tensorator at (O_Y[1],K), e tensor identity, and c_Z(F(K)). This asserts the connecting-map equality, not an isomorphism of triangles or distinguishedness.

source.place: Lemma 20.27.1, exact derived pullback computed on K-flat complexes; translated-unit tensorator normalization, parent node step 3, expanded by the agent.

proof.text: Obtain a counit ε₀ invertible on K-flat representatives from the existing counit-data theorem. Discard its unrelated shifted-unit comparison.

Apply the counit shift-adjustment theorem to ε₀. It gives a natural automorphism a of Qh followed by derived pullback and a shifted-unit isomorphism e such that ε=a.hom followed by ε₀ satisfies the translated-unit shift square. Every ε component at a K-flat representative is invertible, by composition with a component of a.

Apply naturality of ε to the cone projection C.mor₃, then compose with the target shift comparison. Substitute the shift square at C.obj₁. Expand the two localized triangles, rewrite functoriality of composition and associativity. This gives exactly the requested cone connecting-map equality. The proof does not use the cone-equality theorem as an imported dependency.
